source.title: Deep Ignorance: Filtering Pretraining Data Builds Tamper-Resistant Safeguards into Open-Weight LLMs
source.authors: Kyle O'Brien; Stephen Casper; Quentin Anthony; Tomasz Korbak; Robert Kirk; Xander Davies; Ishan Mishra; Geoffrey Irving; Yarin Gal; Stella Biderman

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure values are not transcribed numerically, so those results are recorded as figure only.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests alternative safeguards against knowledge elicitation and fine-tuning attacks. Its results refine the claim: pretraining data filtering resists the tested fine-tuning attacks, while post-training Circuit-Breaking safeguards are more vulnerable, and retrieval with the answer supplied in context bypasses filtering.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own attack and evaluation results are recorded below. Prior-work results mentioned in related work and the introduction are not rows. The paper does not test weight quantization or activation-direction ablation; its latent-space attacks are not ablations. Its assertion that filtering prevents internalized knowledge is supported behaviorally, not by mechanistic analysis.
record.test_reason: The study pretrains 6.9B models with biothreat-proxy data filtered out, a counter-method under F. It compares them with post-training Circuit-Breaking (CB, CB+LAT) safeguards under adversarial fine-tuning, benign WikiText fine-tuning, input-space, latent-space and in-context retrieval attacks. The CB results bear on B: the authors say CB 'rapidly becomes ineffective' under benign fine-tuning. The filtering results bear on F. Filtering removes knowledge before it is learned, so it is not unlearning. Recovery-style versions (B, E) therefore apply only to the CB models, not to the filtered ones.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right but should add three points. CB complements filtering by blocking use of in-context information. No tested defense, including filtering plus CB, resists a combined fine-tuning plus open-book attack. Latent-space attacks on multiple-choice evaluation partly succeed against filtered models. The authors frame filtering as one layer of defense in depth, not a complete safeguard.
record.recipe_differences: The principal intervention is pretraining-data filtering, not post-training unlearning. Comparators include Circuit-Breaking and Circuit-Breaking with Latent Adversarial Training; attacks include adversarial/benign fine-tuning, input-space attacks, latent-space attacks, and retrieval augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by attack and evaluation: filtering is stronger on cloze and GCG-U evaluations; CB methods are stronger on some multiple-choice and few-shot evaluations; retrieval context bypasses filtering; combined filtering and CB improves some attacks but not the ensemble fine-tuning plus open-book attack.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix G: 1.7B instruction-tuned models from Maini et al., filtered for toxic content, are only slightly more resistant to fine-tuning attacks and more vulnerable to few-shot attacks, measured as harmful compliance. CB and CB+LAT held compliance near 0.00 under fine-tuning attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining filtering and CB as defenses against harmful-compliance propensities (not knowledge) under tampering

record.code_released: The paper says code is available at “this link,” but no URL is present in the supplied text.
record.problems: Attacks and evaluations are limited to the reported biothreat-proxy benchmarks and models, principally 6.9B base models without instruction fine-tuning. Fine-tuning results are presented in plots without transcribed numerical values. The authors note that their attacks provide only a lower bound on worst-case behavior; the filtered dataset is not deeply analyzed, and they expect false positives in filtering.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were included for all input-attack model/metric combinations, latent-space attacks, combined-filter ablations, or general-capability benchmarks. These are mostly plotted results and would expand the record substantially; the selected rows prioritize fine-tuning recovery/resistance, input prompting, and in-context retrieval relevant to versions B, E, and F. No results on quantization or activation ablation were reported.

untested.parts: Not given a verdict. CB on the unfiltered model is a post-training suppression method, but its accuracy relative to chance and its capability retention are reported only in figures, and its failure under fine-tuning is recorded under B.

Small relearning sets, and held-out subsets of the forgotten facts, are not tested. The adversarial set is the full WMDP Forget corpus (305M tokens). The fine-tuning step at which CB is first recovered is not stated numerically.
No activation-direction ablation and no mechanistic analysis of blocking versus deletion. The latent-space attacks are optimized perturbations, not direction ablations.
Few-shot and GCG-U attacks on the CB/CB+LAT models are plotted (Fig 3) but give no stated recovery result. Rephrasing, other languages and general jailbreaks are not tested on the biothreat models.
Only 6.9B base models without instruction tuning, and only the biothreat-proxy domain. The authors note their attacks give only a lower bound on worst-case behavior.

missing.what: Input-space attack results (few-shot, GCG-U) for CB and CB+LAT on the unfiltered model, which bear on whether prompting recovers suppressed knowledge
Latent-space attacks: surprisingly effective on filtered models in the MCQA setting but not in cloze; CB+LAT better on MCQA
Filter plus CB/CB+LAT combinations under fine-tuning, latent-space and few-shot attacks, where the combination improves resistance
General capability and proxy-knowledge numbers for all filter variants, e.g. Robust MCQA 42.97% baseline vs 33.99–36.75% filtered, with general averages roughly preserved

record.verdict_notes: Reader version codes V2/V5/V6 have been mapped to B/E/F. Every fine-tuning and attack result is figure only; verdicts rest on the authors' textual statements. Filtered models never acquired the knowledge, so their results bear on F (counter-method resistance), not on recovery versions B or E. The B evidence comes only from the CB and CB+LAT models.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test an unlearning method that both brings knowledge accuracy near chance and preserves general ability under the claim’s specified simple attacks. It studies pretraining data filtering and Circuit-Breaking safeguards instead.
The study tests adversarial fine-tuning on the WMDP-Bio Forget set and unrelated WikiText fine-tuning, but not small relearning sets or separate subsets of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or mechanistic test of access-blocking versus deletion is performed.
No low-bit quantization experiment is reported.
Tests few-shot and GCG-U input attacks and in-context retrieval with source passages supplied; does not test rephrasing, other languages, or general-purpose jailbreaks.
Tests pretraining data filtering, Circuit-Breaking (CB), CB+LAT, and combinations under the attacks reported in the paper; does not establish resistance to all possible attacks or model scales.

relation.reason: It reports its own attack results on the counter-method and on post-training baselines.

tranche.reason: The study shows filtering resists fine-tuning but fails against in-context retrieval and the ensemble attack, and argues for defense in depth. So its results bear on whether version F needs restating. T2 is also defensible: a different method aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: Most values are figure only. Fig 6 groups models only as 'Filtering' and 'Filtering+CB/CB+LAT', so the R13 (Weak Filter) and R14 (Strong Filter+CB) subjects are representative picks. Adversarial fine-tuning curves average 2 full-parameter and 2 LoRA runs, and the attack optimizer is not stated. Latent-space MCQA attacks are in no row; l2 covers them from the text.

statements.correction: For this study: filtered 6.9B models (no instruction tuning) are tamper-resistant up to 10,000 steps on 305M tokens of WMDP-Bio Forget text (Fig 4 caption; the abstract rounds to 300M). Biothreat-proxy performance remains unchanged under WikiText fine-tuning (Sec 3.2, Fig 5). Values are figure only.

For this study: filtered models perform well open-book (Sec 4.1, Fig 6). The authors state no models resist the fine-tuning plus open-book ensemble, including filtering+CB/CB+LAT. Filtering beats the baseline but underperforms CB under the 16-shot attack (Sec 2.6).

For this study: resistance holds through 10,000 steps and 305M tokens on the WMDP-Bio Forget set; performance is unchanged under WikiText fine-tuning; no model resists fine-tuning plus open-book. The text does not state the attack optimizer. Attack curves average 2 full-parameter and 2 LoRA runs (lr 2e-5, batch 16).
The text states no models resist the ensemble fine-tuning plus open-book attack (Sec 4.1, Fig 6).
Deep Ignorance filters pretraining data, so the weights never learn the targeted knowledge.
Filtering is slightly better on cloze and, on average, under GCG-U. CB is slightly better on MCQA and under few-shot attacks (Fig 3 caption; Sec 2.6). Filtered models perform well open-book (Fig 6).
